messages:
emma: FYI customer reported a big invoice delta this month vs their SDK estimates. They say prompt+completion totals from our API are ~3x higher than what their client-side estimator reports.

devon: Can you share the example request and the invoice lines? usually it's system messages or tool/function tokens getting omitted on client side.

emma: pasted the minimal repro they sent:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXXX' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize X"}], "stream": false}'
```

emma: Their SDK estimator (client) computed ~240 tokens. Server returned usage: prompt=820, completion=30. Invoice matched server usage.

maria: Any chance they're not counting system tokens (or hidden tool/system injections)? our meter counts every token processed by the runtime, including injected moderation/system/context and any tool payloads.

alex: I pulled the invoice and meter logs for that customer_id. I see a series of internal "assistant.system" messages injected by the private routing policy (policy: add-tenant-context) in the request path — those add ~500 tokens across the batch.

devon: Interesting. Did the SDK estimator run tokenizer on the pre-send payload or the post-route payload? If it only tokenizes the user-visible messages it will undercount.

emma: Customer says SDK does tokenize pre-send payload only. They didn't expect server-side additions.

maria: This is a known edge case. Two sources of delta we typically see:
1) Server-side injected messages (policies, moderation, routing labels, tool prompts).
2) Streaming truncation/rounding differences — meter charges per emitted token and our streaming logic may flush extra tokens in chunk boundaries.

sre-bot: deploy-billing-patch v2026.03 applied to meter-service on stable region at 2026-03-15T02:14Z — added header X-Server-Injected-Token-Count for diagnostics.

devon: Steps to repro for engineering/customer:
- Capture the exact request body sent from SDK (pre-send)
- Request the server-side echoed payload via support endpoint (we can pull the post-policy payload from request-id)
- Compare token counts using our tokenizer on both payloads

emma: I asked the customer for a request-id and sent them temporary script to collect both counts. They replied with request-id: req_0a9f3 and attached pre/post payload diffs.

alex: Looking at req_0a9f3: pre-send tokens=238, post-policy tokens=763, injected tokens=525. Meter shows prompt=763, completion=29. Invoice matches meter.

maria: Proposed mitigation for SDK: add an optional server_overhead_estimate that uses conservative rule-of-thumb (+20%-+200 tokens depending on routing features) OR call a new endpoint /v1/debug/echo that returns post-policy token_count (limited access).

emma: Customer is OK with a one-time billing credit for the month if we can confirm they weren't abusing. Any objections?

devon: +1. Also we should update docs and add a short FAQ: "Why does my SDK estimator differ from invoice?" — explain server-side injections, function/tool tokens, streaming rounding.

alex: Credit issued $450, logged under billing ticket BT-4532. Customer notified.

maria: I'll open a small SDK patch to expose a helper computeServerVisibleTokenEstimate() and add docs. Also add example showing how server-side moderation/tool tokens can increase usage.

emma: Thanks — closing loop with customer now. :thumbsup:
